title: Edge cache price sensitivity and SKU split notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick experimental workbook + recommendations for how an edge LRU cache layer (prefix and response-level caching) and a model SKU split (small/medium/large families) change hosted API per-token COGS and margins by region. This doc is intentionally lightweight — working notes and sample cells for the full spreadsheet we should build (see linked repo).

Context and motivation:
- We continue to see 20–40% of tokens generated being repeating prefixes (chat history, system prompts). Small amounts of cache hit improvement can materially improve per-token marginal COGS at scale.
- Product is considering a SKU split that would route lower-latency, short-sequence requests to smaller cheaper SKUs, and long-form completions to larger SKUs. We need a simple sensitivity table to show trade-offs for finance and Sales.

Key assumptions (baseline):
- Base GPU execution cost per model-token (no cache):
  - small-family: $0.00018/token
  - medium-family: $0.00032/token
  - large-family: $0.00094/token
- Edge cache hit is applied to token output only; cache hit = response tokens served from cache with near-zero GPU cost (network + infra marginal cost ignored for initial model).
- Cache hit rate scenarios: 0%, 10%, 25%, 40% for sensitivity analysis.
- SKU split scenarios: % of traffic routed to small/medium/large (three variants below).
- Hosted price (examples): $0.0009/token (public-facing list price), effective price bundles and enterprise discounts vary.

Mini-sensitivity table (sample numbers, US-WEST):
Region: us-west
Scenario A: current mix (60% medium, 30% large, 10% small), cache hit 10%
- Weighted base COGS = 0.6*0.00032 + 0.3*0.00094 + 0.1*0.00018 = 0.000464
- Effective token COGS with 10% cache hit => 0.9*0.000464 = 0.0004176
- Margin at $0.0009 price => (0.0009 - 0.0004176)/0.0009 = 53.6%

Scenario B: aggressive SKU split (80% small, 15% medium, 5% large), cache hit 25%
- Weighted base COGS = 0.8*0.00018 + 0.15*0.00032 + 0.05*0.00094 = 0.000245
- Effective token COGS with 25% cache hit => 0.75*0.000245 = 0.00018375
- Margin at $0.0009 price => 79.6%

Scenario C: legacy mix (20% small, 50% medium, 30% large), cache hit 0%
- Weighted base COGS = 0.2*0.00018 + 0.5*0.00032 + 0.3*0.00094 = 0.000482
- Effective token COGS with 0% cache hit => 0.000482
- Margin at $0.0009 price => 46.4%

Regional delta examples (rough):
- eu-west: GPU pricing ~+12% (power + amortization) => multiply COGS by 1.12 baseline.
- ap-south: GPU pricing ~+25% => multiply by 1.25.
- us-central: baseline multiplier ~1.02.
-> This changes required cache hit / sku mix to meet target margin thresholds in region (see next).

Sensitivity insights (short takeaways):
1) Small changes in cache hit rate (10 -> 25%) yield larger % improvements when the SKU mix is medium/large heavy. Why: cache reduces the expensive tail tokens more effectively when they dominate cost.
2) SKU split is the highest-leverage knob for hosted margins if product patterns allow routing (short-chat vs long-form). A 20–30% shift towards small-family drastically reduces weighted COGS.
3) Regional multipliers mean APAC and EU need higher cache hit or higher price to maintain parity on margin. E.g., a 12% increase in COGS requires ~3–4% more cache hit (absolute) or a ~0.00005/higher price to break even.
4) Operational note: aggressive SKU split increases policy complexity (routing, cold-start risk, and customer-perceived latency). We must model latency SLO tradeoffs.

Quick recommended SKU-split experiments to run (A/B style):
- Experiment 1 (short-window): Route 25% of early-returning short prompt flows (<128 context) to small-family for 2 weeks; measure token-level COGS, latency, and error rate. Ticket: JIRA-OPT-413.
- Experiment 2 (cache priming): Enable aggressive prefix caching for top-5000 common prompts in us-west for 7 days — measure cache hit and downstream COGS. Ticket: JIRA-OPT-416.
- Experiment 3 (regional price lift): Run a controlled price lift in APAC test account cohort to measure demand elasticity and required margin recovery.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need more realistic network + CDN marginal cost per cached response (currently ignored). Add rough $/request to model.
- Work with SRE to estimate cache operational cost (invalidation, storage) and failure modes.
- Build full spreadsheet (tabbed): assumptions, regional multipliers, SKU mixes, cache sensitivity grid, revenue/price elasticity layer, and break-even waterfall.
- Validate model token distribution (seq length histogram) with analytics team — this heavily influences effective savings.

Deliverables and next steps:
- Miguel: prototype the simulation notebook (edge-cache-sim) and push sample CSV by Jan 28.
- Priya: coordinate SRE numbers for cache infra cost by Feb 5.
- Ava: assemble a 2-page executive one-pager with two recommended pilot experiments and expected P&L impact for review with finance (due Feb 10).

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally rough. The aim is a quick decision-grade sensitivity table for prioritizing edge cache work and SKU routing. If we see >15% improvement in weighted COGS for realistic mixes, we should prioritize pilot.

References and quick links:
- cache simulation code: github.com/redwood/optimize/edge-cache-sim
- related ticket: JIRA-OPT-412 (edge cache concept)
